skill.name: asana-automation
skill.description: Automate Asana tasks, projects, sections, teams, and users through Rube MCP and the Composio Asana toolkit.
skill.summary: Guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Asana automation workflows using Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The shell-execution and system-reconnaissance static findings are false positives caused by Markdown tool names, code fences, and Asana GID terminology. The real issue is a disclosed third-party MCP and OAuth dependency, which creates a low-risk trust boundary for Asana data.

remediation.issue: Third-party MCP endpoint requires trust in an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Document that Rube MCP is a third-party service. Tell users to review OAuth scopes and use a least-privileged Asana account.

remediation.issue: Write and bulk workflows can change Asana data.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before create, move, duplicate, or parallel request operations. Preview target GIDs and expected changes first.

- `projects`: Array of project GIDs to add task to
1. `ASANA_SUBMIT_PARALLEL_REQUESTS` - Execute multiple API calls in parallel [Required]
- `actions`: Array of action objects with method, path, and data
- Asana uses cursor-based pagination with `offset` parameter
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Each action must be a valid Asana API call

content.user_title: Automate Asana Workflows with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Teams lose time creating tasks, resolving project IDs, and moving work across Asana projects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for Asana tasks, projects, teams, and sections.
actual_capabilities: Guides Rube MCP connection setup and Asana OAuth checks.
Resolves workspace, project, task, section, team, and user GIDs before actions.
Creates and retrieves Asana tasks, subtasks, projects, sections, and project task lists.
Lists workspace projects, teams, team members, users, and current user records.
Uses Asana parallel requests for bulk API operations when the schema supports them.
Explains pagination, workspace scoping, and GID formatting.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP tools and an active Asana connection.
Does not provide Asana credentials or bypass OAuth permissions.
Tool schemas may change, so the agent must search current tools first.
Bulk operations do not roll back successful requests when another request fails.

use_cases.title: Create Project Tasks
use_cases.description: Create tasks and subtasks after resolving the correct workspace and project identifiers.

use_cases.title: Organize Work by Section
use_cases.description: List project sections and move tasks into the right stage with confirmed task and section GIDs.

use_cases.title: Review Teams and Workspaces
use_cases.description: Find workspace teams, users, and current account details before assigning work.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Asana Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to verify Rube MCP availability. Check the Asana toolkit connection and tell me what authorization step is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Task Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Asana task for <work item> in <project> due <date>. Resolve the workspace and project GIDs, then confirm details before creation.

prompt_templates.title: Move Tasks Between Sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Review project <project name>. List its sections and move task <task name or GID> into <section name> after resolving all IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Bulk Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a bulk Asana update for these tasks: <list>. Search current tool schemas, show proposed parallel actions, and wait for approval.

output_examples.input: Create a task for the launch checklist in the Marketing project due Friday.
output_examples.output: Workspace and project were resolved. The task is ready for confirmation with due date, project placement, and optional assignee.

output_examples.input: Move the onboarding task into the In Review section.
output_examples.output: The project sections were listed, the task and section GIDs were matched, and the move is ready for approval.

output_examples.input: List teams and users in my workspace before assigning project work.
output_examples.output: The workspace teams and users were retrieved so assignments can use verified user identifiers.

best_practices: Search current Rube tool schemas before each workflow.
Confirm workspace, project, task, and section GIDs before write actions.
Review OAuth permissions and use least-privileged Asana accounts.
anti_patterns: Running write operations before resolving the workspace and project.
Using stale tool parameters without checking current schemas.
Submitting bulk requests without previewing each action and rollback expectations.

faq.question: Does this skill connect directly to Asana?
faq.answer: It uses Rube MCP and the Composio Asana toolkit. Users still need an active Asana OAuth connection.

faq.question: Can it create and move tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents task creation, subtask creation, section moves, and project task listing.

faq.question: Why does it search tool schemas first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP tool schemas can change. Searching first helps the agent use current parameter names and requirements.

faq.question: Does it support bulk Asana actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers parallel Asana requests, but users should preview each action before execution.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: Permissions depend on the Asana OAuth connection and workspace access. Use the minimum account permissions needed for the workflow.

faq.question: Can it bypass Asana approval or access controls?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the authenticated Asana connection and cannot bypass Asana permissions.
